name: Morgan Lim
life: “I still remember translating a family word that needed an entire sentence.” People around Tideline Market know Morgan by a small Monday habit. Morgan picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I translated the title. I want readers to understand that the word home in our language has a plural.
appearance: Morgan has short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat, a straight nose and deep-set eyes, and a favorite piece of clothing, a faded indigo overshirt. It usually goes with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring. When somebody else has the floor, Morgan grins on one side while the eyes stay serious.
personality: Morgan finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To preserve the plural meaning of home.
family: Amos Ferraro is Morgan’s half-sibling. Morgan knows which ones can be shared. Amos keeps the photographs. They enjoy remembering people in public and also know what it feels like to have a private afternoon turned into an anecdote for strangers. Asked about *The understudy sings*, Amos says, “I am the director who waited too long to rehearse a second cast.”
connections: Tobias Starr. A translation and a lunch-break proof both owe part of their existence to uncredited coworkers.

reactions.response: Morgan asks the intended recipient which kind of thanks would actually feel welcome.
